extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, MER co-directors, program evaluators, and mathematics department leaders/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation guidance and criteria for assessing the Mathematicians and Education Reform Forum (MER), including metrics of individual and departmental impact, methodological standards for evaluation, and program design/selection criteria. Focus is on how MER facilitates mathematics education reform and how to judge its effectiveness and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of educational issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether participants feel more aware of issues in mathematics education as a result of MER (e.g., calculus reform, use of technology, mathematicians’ involvement in education reform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey respondents reported percentages (e.g., >70% of mathematicians and K-12 educators, >50% of math-educators) feeling more aware. Open-ended responses identified the most frequently cited topics. Use both closed-item awareness questions and open-ended coding to capture specific issues raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a supportive atmosphere for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether MER creates a supportive professional environment that builds relationships among mathematicians and others interested in education reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use items such as reported comfort contacting MER colleagues about professional matters (noted as >70% agreement). Consider qualitative indicators of networking and collegial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in individual classroom pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether individual participants report changes in their own teaching attributable to MER involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify percent reporting changed teaching (e.g., ~50% of mathematicians). Capture types of pedagogical changes (cooperative learning, incorporation of technology like graphing calculators and software, hands-on activities, increased participation, reformed curricula, new assessments). Note that some may attribute change indirectly or see changes as inevitable but still influenced by MER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental attitudes toward educational reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess shifts in departmental culture regarding the value and acceptance of educational reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include percent who feel educational reform is highly valued or accepted (report: >50% highly valued; ~75% at least accepted). Primary indicators: improvements in curricula, attention to better pedagogy, and increased institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of curricular improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure concrete curricular changes at department level (e.g., adoption of reform calculus programs, development of entry-level or graduate courses focused on pedagogy, remedial education reform, re-writing pre-service programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific program adoptions (Harvard Calculus cited), new courses, and curricular redesigns as direct evidence of departmental reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether educational initiatives have institutional backing sufficient for long-term sustainability (beyond a few committed faculty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for institutionalization signals: multiple faculty involved, administrative support, continuity after key individuals depart. Note anti-pattern: initiatives resting on very few faculty (risk of faltering if they leave).

rubrics_metrics.name: MER as a support mechanism (realistic effectiveness standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat MER’s effectiveness primarily as its ability to support and sustain members already involved in education efforts rather than as a direct cause of widespread change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluators recommend incorporating this conception of effectiveness because many participants were 'already involved' prior to joining MER; using a stricter causal-change standard would be unrealistic for voluntary networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of inter-departmental collaboration and concrete outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether MER workshops and networking produce collaborative projects (e.g., planning grants, interdisciplinary initiatives), graduate student exchanges, internships, shared computer-based projects, or databases for comparative information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples that emerged from workshops (Nebraska–Oklahoma planning grant; graduate/post-doc exchanges). Track whether workshop ideas were adopted and implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and structure of workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate workshop design features that maximize positive outcomes (overarching theme, breakout sessions for specific interests, informal contact time such as meals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants praised workshops for structuring time to promote 'bouncing ideas' and building comfort quickly. Consider assessing thematic coherence, breakout usefulness, and built-in informal interaction opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between prescriptiveness and non-prescriptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether MER strikes an appropriate balance between prescribing reforms (which may alienate mathematicians) and being too vague (which may accomplish little).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MER is commended for 'walking the fine line' by gently adding ideas. Evaluate participant receptivity and recruitment/retention outcomes as evidence of correct balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of program focus (alignment with member expertise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether MER focuses its efforts where its members have the most to offer (noting MER’s emphasis on postsecondary reform even when initial intent was pre-college).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the match between MER activities and participants' expertise; consider coordination with K-12 organizations to connect efforts across levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Network membership/selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to select departments for the Departmental Network: outstanding research departments, commitment to educational reform, primarily research universities (to model others), invited by Task Force/Advisory Committee knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership operationalized by a three-year commitment, sending a team to yearly workshops, maintaining communication via e-mail network, and trying to spread interest within their departments. Inclusion is selective and based on perceived leadership in education reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/participation screening via letter of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that individual workshop applicants submit a letter of support from their department chair or dean as an up-front assurance of departmental support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-directors view this requirement as part of candidate screening and as a mechanism to connect MER work to departmental structures and systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year commitment and operationalization for departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments in the Network are expected to make a three-year commitment expressed through team participation in workshops and ongoing communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalization includes team attendance at annual departmental workshops, maintenance of e-mail communication channels, and internal dissemination efforts to involve more faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of triangulation and mixed methods in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ multiple data sources and mixed qualitative/quantitative methodologies (e.g., NSF Program Officer, co-directors, workshops, task force meetings, surveys, interviews, participant-observation, document review; coding/domain analyses and descriptive/inferential statistics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate findings across data sources. For qualitative material use coding and domain analyses; for survey data use descriptive and inferential statistics as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant-observation and site visits standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Include participant-observation at multiple MER events and case-study site visits to departments, using both pre-ordinate checklists and responsive approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers alternated attendance at meetings; site visits included interviews with chairs, grad students, 'pro-MER'/'neutral'/'anti-MER' faculty, attending reformed classes. Use a priori checklists (documents to review) but remain flexible to site-specific themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey population and sampling rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey the entire known population of past and current MER participants (730 people) rather than sampling, because subgroup membership (mathematicians, math-educators, K-12 teachers) could not be reliably identified for stratified sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveying the entire population aimed to maximize inclusion of smaller subgroups (K-12 teachers and mathematics educators). Note trade-offs versus probabilistic sampling and implications for representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing and stakeholder collaboration in instrument development
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot instruments with MER co-directors, advisory committee, and task force members to 'learn the language' and ensure questions are mutually understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreters collaborated on each draft; co-directors commented on drafts. Objective: produce instruments that reflect participant terminology and are contextually appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail/network communication design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of departmental e-mail listserver: original plan limited subscriptions to a few faculty liaisons who moderate and forward; evaluators suggest opening list to any interested individuals in departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original approach prevents over-mailing and proselytizing; suggested change intended to relieve liaisons, increase traffic, and engage more participants. Low traffic observed implies little danger of flooding mailboxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of departmental awareness and internal dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the degree to which department faculty know about MER and understand the implications of membership; link to liaison activity and departmental interest in education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data showed generally less than half of faculty had heard of MER and fewer understood implications. Evaluate effectiveness of liaisons in spreading information and consider inviting skeptics to workshops to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of initiative collapse due to concentrated responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and measure risk when pre-college or K-12 initiatives rest on very few faculty members rather than being department-wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence from case (Penn State) where departure of a key individual led to collapse of initiatives. Use this as a criterion to push for broader institutionalization.
